turns.content: For clinical-scale production of a therapeutic mRNA before lipid-nanoparticle encapsulation, compare mammalian-cell expression with cell-free in vitro transcription. Which upstream route is appropriate, and why?
For the chosen route, what form should the DNA template take? Also explain why treating the product with RNase before purification would be incompatible with recovering intact mRNA.
The desired transcript is polyadenylated. Which affinity capture method can exploit that feature, and what molecular interaction makes it selective?
After capture, which chromatography mode can polish IVT mRNA, and which truncated or double-stranded RNA impurities can it help separate?
Combine the upstream synthesis, product-integrity, affinity-capture, and polishing choices into one process flow.
Why does a poly(A) tail enable oligo-dT capture, and how would an unpolyadenylated product change the purification strategy?
Compare this flow with mammalian-cell production, RNase cleavage, size-only separation, and anion-exchange capture in terms of integrity and selectivity.
How confidently can this architecture be recommended without data on impurity loads, resin capacity, recovery, clearance, and release analytics?
Report the final process flow and the role of the linearized template, oligo-dT capture, and hydrophobic-interaction polishing.
